zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two or more attribute values (e.g., "Alice is the person who uses a Huawei P50"), immediately record that equivalence and propagate it to all other constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Apply as soon as a clue contains a direct equality between a name and another attribute, or between two non‑name attributes.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt treated the equivalence as separate facts and later assigned a different phone to Alice, causing a contradiction.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue pins an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., "The root‑beer lover is in the second house"), set that attribute to that house right away and eliminate it from all other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a specific house number.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt ignored the fixed‑position clue and later placed the root‑beer drinker elsewhere, causing a conflict.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Adjacency clues ('next to', 'directly left of', 'directly right of') require the two referenced houses to be immediate neighbors, with the correct left/right orientation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses adjacency language.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt treated "Eric and the cat lover are next to each other" as a non‑adjacent relationship and placed them two houses apart.

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: The verifier expects a JSON object with a "header" array listing column names and a "rows" array of house entries; any deviation (e.g., extra keys, missing header) leads to rejection.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt wrapped the table inside a "solution" key, which the verifier did not recognize.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: The model has a limited token budget; overly long reasoning can cause the final JSON to be cut off, resulting in an incomplete answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the reasoning phase, keep explanations brief and place the final JSON at the very end.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt produced a very long chain of deductions, and the verifier received only a truncated JSON, causing failure.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Attribute values must be reproduced exactly as given (including case, spaces, punctuation); any deviation (e.g., "OnePlus 9" vs "oneplus 9") leads to mismatch.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final table, copy attribute strings verbatim from the puzzle description.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt wrote "OnePlus 9" with capital letters, while the expected token was "oneplus 9", causing a mismatch.

zebralogic.title: Interpret Directional Ordering Correctly
zebralogic.principle: For any clue containing "somewhere to the right of" or "somewhere to the left of", enforce a strict ordering (house(X) < house(Y) for "left of"), but not necessarily adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing ordering clues that do not specify "directly".
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt treated "The Xiaomi Mi 11 is somewhere to the left of the water drinker" as an adjacency constraint, placing them next to each other incorrectly.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "The person who has black hair is not in the sixth house"), eliminate that attribute from that house immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a negative positional statement.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt placed black hair in house 6 despite the explicit exclusion.

zebralogic.title: Transitive Ordering Inference
zebralogic.principle: When multiple direct ordering clues form a chain (e.g., A left of B and B left of C), infer the implied ordering (A left of C) to reduce possibilities.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After collecting all ordering clues, compute the transitive closure.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt failed to deduce that the Xiaomi Mi 11 must be left of Bob because it is left of water and water is left of Bob.

zebralogic.title: Distinguish Overlapping Attribute Categories
zebralogic.principle: When a puzzle contains multiple attribute categories that share value names (e.g., "cat" appears in both Animal and Pet), interpret each clue in the context of the category explicitly mentioned; if the clue does not specify a category, infer the intended category based on phrasing (e.g., "has a cat" refers to the Animal category, while "pet cat" refers to the Pet category).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a value that exists in more than one attribute set.
zebralogic.example: A rejected attempt assigned "cat" to the wrong category, swapping the Animal and Pet assignments for the fifth house, because the clue "The person who has a cat is in the fifth house" was interpreted as referring to the Pet category instead of Animal.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to be exhaustive, but the token limit cuts off the tail of the output.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise, place the final JSON at the very end, and limit explanatory text.

zebralogic.description: Providing the solution in a format not recognized by the verifier.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Model follows natural language habits instead of the strict JSON structure required.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Produce exactly a JSON object with "header" and "rows" keys, no extra nesting or keys.

zebralogic.description: Using incorrect case or synonyms for attribute values.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Model normalizes text or guesses alternative spellings.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings verbatim from the puzzle description, preserving case, spaces, and punctuation.

zebralogic.description: Confusing overlapping attribute categories (e.g., Animal vs Pet) leading to misassignment of values.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Ambiguity in clue phrasing and the model's tendency to treat values as globally unique across categories.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Track each attribute category separately; use the exact wording of clues to decide which category a value belongs to.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: Confusion between strict ordering and adjacency, or reversing left/right direction.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "somewhere to the left of" only imposes house(X) < house(Y); adjacency requires "directly left of" or "next to".
